faqs.q: Should I repair my gutters or get new gutters for my Montclair home?

runs.v: Fix the run when the damage stays localized to a seam, hanger, or section; choose replacement when corrosion or failures recur across the run, because neglected gutters can cause leaks and structural damage over time.

faqs.q: What gutter material works best on a Montclair Victorian or Tudor?

runs.v: Copper half-round gutters, which last 50-plus years and read as period-correct; seamless aluminum costs less and suits Colonial Revival and Craftsman homes.

faqs.q: How often should gutters be cleaned in Montclair?

runs.v: At least twice a year, in spring and fall, and every three months for homes surrounded by dense trees, per Angi and GAF maintenance guidance. Clogged gutters can lead to mold growth and water damage, gutter cleaning prevents foundation erosion and basement flooding, and gutter guards prevent debris accumulation.

faqs.q: Do clogged gutters cause ice dams on a Montclair roof?

runs.v: Water trapped in clogged gutters can freeze and worsen eave ice, leading to leaks, but the root cause is attic heat melting snow that refreezes at the cold eave, per University of Minnesota Extension; an ice barrier at least 24 inches inside the exterior wall line protects the edge, per IRC Section R905.1.2.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for gutter work in Montclair?

runs.v: Not on a detached one- or two-family home, where gutter work is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7. A commercial, multi-family, attached, historic-district, or landmark property can need a permit or extra review, so confirm with the Montclair construction office first.
